items.title: George Benson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He called one of his friends that was [?], this young boy. Stanley Banks was his name. He brought him to rehearsal. Stanley was a kid. He was only 23 years old.

ctx.x: Were you listening to other kinds of music at this time? You came . . .

I was listening to everything. I was listening to guitar records. I listened to Charlie Parker records, Art Tatum records, and other musicians who we would go to town and we’d go to their jam sessions or their gigs, and I’d hear what they were playing, all the organ players. That was what we came from, the organ era. So, Jimmy Smith, Jack McDuff, Johnny “Hammond” Smith, and quite a few, Jimmy McGriff and Groove Holmes. These were all still our favorite guys.

But the world was changing. The organ was going away. Piano was coming in. So I started – the greatest thing happened to me. There was a young genius organ player from Buffalo, New York. I met him when he was 15, and I knew he was going to be a great player. But his – I went home and met his folks. His mother begged me. She said, “Mr. Benson, don’t take my son out of here.
